newsitem.title: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES: SOCCER-JAPAN BEAT UZBEKISTAN 4-0 TO REACH LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAPAN BEAT UZBEKISTAN 4-0 TO REACH LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Rising star Masakiyo Maezono scored two late goals as defending champions Japan scored a comfortable 4-0 (halftime 2-0) over Uzbekistan in an Asian Cup group C match on Monday and a quarter-final berth.
Japan, favourites to regain the title, controlled the game throughout and were well worth their victory over a team that won the gold medal at the Asian Games two years ago.
Maezono put more respectability to the scoreline, grabbing his goals in the final four minutes.
His first came from a 20-metre free kick which he lobbed over an Uzbek defensive wall and into the net. His second was a gem.
Running on to a long ball from midfield, he flicked the ball over an advancing keeper and then rolled it into an open net.
Japanese ace Kazuyoshi Miura showed glimpses of his magic throughout and opened his account at the championships with Japan's second goal.

The holders, who beat Syria 2-1 in their opening match, now have six points and a guaranteed quarter-final place in the 12-nation tournament. The fate of Uzbekistan, who had beaten China 2-1, depends on the outcome of their match with Syria on Wednesday.
China were to play Syria later on Monday.
Japan began the match on the offensive and needed only seven minutes to take the lead.
Striker Hiroshi Nanami pounced on a loose ball outside the Uzbek penalty area and hit a 25-metre drive into the left corner of Bugalo Pavel's goal.

Uzbekistan were restricted to counterattacks which could have produced an equaliser in the 16th minute but for a fine save by Japanese keeper Kenichi Shimokawa from a fierce shot by midfielder Lebedev Sergey.
Defender Gennadi Denisov kept Uzbekistan in the game in the 29th minute when he twice cleared off the line from Hiroaki Morishima who had rounded the keeper after a neat pass by Maezono.
Uzbekistan lived dangerously until the 37th minute when Miura headed in from one meter out after keeper Pavel parried a close-range shot from Takuya Takagi.
Miura dazzled the Uzbek defence with some neat footwork in the second half but his final touch let him down. He saw his fierce left foot shot in the 71st minute well saved by Pavel.
Uzbekistan repeatedly caught the Japanese forwards off side but could not trouble the Japanese defence and never looked like scoring.

Japan: 19-Kenichi Shimokawa; 2-Hiroshige Yanagimoto, 3-Naoki Soma, 4-Masami Ihara, 5-Norio Omura; 6-Motohiro Yamaguchi, 8- Masakiyo Maezono, 9-Takuya Takagi (14-Masayuki Okanu 75), 10- Hiroshi Nanami; 11-Kazauyoshi Miura; 15-Hiroaki Morishima (7- Yasuto Honda 73).

Uzbekistan: 1-Pavel Bugalo; 2-Fevzi Davletov (20-Dilmurod Nazarov 46), 4-Farkhad Magametov, 5-Eduard Momotov (14-Nikolay Shirshov 67), 6-Ilkhom Sharipov, 7-Stepan Atayan; 8-Sergey Lebedev, 9-Ravshan Bazarov; 10-Igor Shkvyrin; 16-Gennady Denisov; 17-Numon Khasanov (19-Abduraimov Azamat 67).
